steps.title: What is an e-reader?
steps.body: An e-reader is a device for reading digital books (e-books), such as a Kobo or Kindle. The screen looks like paper and is easy on the eyes, even outside in sunlight.

steps.title: Finding and downloading a book
steps.body:
1. Open the store app on your e-reader, or borrow free e-books through your library's app
  2. Search by title, author, or topic
  3. Click 'Download' or 'Borrow' — the book appears automatically in your bookshelf

steps.title: Adjusting the font size
steps.body: Tap the middle of the screen while reading to open the menu. Choose the letter icon (often 'Aa') to adjust the font size, typeface, and line spacing to your liking.

steps.title: What is 'the cloud'?
steps.body: The cloud is storage space on the internet, instead of only on your phone or computer. This keeps your photos safe even if you lose or replace your phone.

steps.title: Backing up photos automatically
steps.body: With an app like Google Photos (Android) or iCloud (iPhone), new photos are automatically saved to the cloud whenever your phone is connected to Wi-Fi. You usually turn this on once in the app's settings.

steps.title: Finding and sharing a photo
steps.body:
1. Open the photos app and search by date, place, or even a keyword (for example 'dog')
  2. Open the photo
  3. Click the share icon to send the photo via, for example, WhatsApp or email

steps.title: Why use a trusted medical website?
steps.body: A website like the Dutch Thuisarts.nl is written by doctors and gives reliable, easy-to-understand information about symptoms and conditions — unlike random internet search results, which aren't always accurate.

steps.title: Looking up symptoms
steps.body:
1. Type your symptom in the search bar, for example 'headache' or 'cold'
  2. Read the explanation of possible causes and what you can do yourself
  3. The bottom of the page usually explains when you should see a doctor

steps.title: When should you still call your doctor?
steps.body: Thuisarts.nl is meant as a helpful tool, not a replacement for a doctor. Always call your doctor (or emergency services if urgent) if you're worried, or if symptoms persist or get worse.

steps.title: What is a password manager?
steps.body: A password manager is an app that securely stores all your passwords in encrypted form. You only need to remember one master password — the app fills in the rest automatically for you.

steps.title: Saving and filling in a password
steps.body:
1. Log in to a website as usual
  2. The password manager asks: 'Save this password?' — click 'Save'
  3. Next time you log in, the app offers to fill in the password automatically

steps.title: Why this is safer
steps.body: Without a password manager, people often use the same (weak) password everywhere — if one website gets hacked, criminals can then access all your accounts. A password manager makes it easy to have a different, strong password for every website, without having to remember them all yourself.
